links.comparator_used: Zero-shot LLM without retrieval (parametric knowledge alone)
links.outcome: Zero-shot medical question answering accuracy on MedQA USMLE
links.effect: Retrieval augmentation significantly improved zero-shot performance; best configuration (dense retrieval with query reformulation and reranking) reached 60.49% accuracy
links.tradeoff: A clear tradeoff between retrieval effectiveness and computational cost; simpler dense retrieval configurations gave strong performance with higher throughput
links.quote: Results show that retrieval augmentation significantly improves zero-shot medical question answering performance.

links.effect: Domain-specialized models better utilized retrieved medical evidence than general-purpose models (no numbers given in the abstract)
